title: Urbanisation: One Chinese City Changes Across the Decades
subject: china-studies

scenes.caption: Stage 1: farmland and a small town
scenes.narration: At the first stage the map is mostly farmland. A small town stands where the roads cross, and only 15 of every 100 people live in the town - the rest live and work in the countryside.

scenes.caption: Stage 2: factories and first housing appear
scenes.narration: Factories are built on farmland at the town's edge, and their jobs pull people in from the countryside. The first housing blocks rise beside them, the built-up area spreads, and the urban share climbs to 38 of every 100 people.

scenes.caption: Stage 3: built-up districts spread outward
scenes.narration: The built-up districts spread outward from the core and the factories, and the farmland shrinks to a strip in the west. Most people now live in the city: the urban share reaches 62 of every 100 people.

scenes.caption: Stage 4: a mostly built-up city, reached in stages
scenes.narration: The city is now mostly built-up: 85 of every 100 people live in urban districts and only a small farmland remnant is left. But it did not happen in one sudden leap - replay the stages and the built-up area grows step by step, exactly as the earlier scenes showed.
